# Self study - Session 2 {#sec-act2-selfstudy2}

In this session, we will revisit the dataset from @{sec-act2}, the **Explainable AI (XAI) Drilling Dataset** by @{wallsberger2023}.
We will explore it in depth, splitting our analysis into four milestones, each building on the previous one.

---

## Milestone 1: Data Acquisition and Understanding {#sec-act2-selfstudy2-m1}

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
::::{#exr-basics-mv-space}
## Register and download the dataset
::::
1. Register on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com).
1. Read the description of the [**Explainable AI (XAI) Drilling Dataset**](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raphaelwallsberger/xai-drilling-dataset/).
1. Download the dataset.
1. Load the dataset into your environment and inspect its structure: number of rows, columns, data types, and any obvious issues.
1. Identify the target variable(s) and any class imbalances.
:::

---

## Milestone 2: Exploratory Data Analysis {#sec-act2-selfstudy2-m2}

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
::::{#exr-basics-mv-space}
## Explore the dataset
::::
1. Pretend that you did not read the _Subgroup failures_ paragraph in the description. Explore the dataset and find insights related to the different failure types.
1. Do your findings align with the description given in the _Subgroup failures_ paragraph?
1. Compute summary statistics for each feature grouped by failure type.
1. Create at least two visualizations (e.g., histograms, box plots) that reveal differences between failure types.
:::

---

## Milestone 3: Deep Dive Visualization {#sec-act2-selfstudy2-m3}

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
::::{#exr-basics-mv-space}
## Visualize failure patterns with plotly
::::
1. Recreate the key visualizations from milestone 2 using `plotly` for interactivity.
1. Create a parallel coordinates plot to explore relationships between multiple features and failure types.
1. Use dropdown widgets to filter the plot by failure type and observe how feature relationships change.
1. Document any new patterns or anomalies discovered through the interactive exploration.
:::

---

## Milestone 4: Reporting Findings {#sec-act2-selfstudy2-m4}

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" collapse="true" icon=false}
::::{#exr-basics-mv-space}
## Generate a polished report with Quarto
::::
1. Polish your document: keep relevant insights, remove unnecessary details, focus on key findings.
1. Document with markdown cells and export the result as HTML or PDF (since your management most likely will not have JupyterLab installed).
   - PDF: The document will be a static version of your notebook, so make sure to include all relevant information and insights directly in the document.
   - HTML: The document will also be a static version of your notebook (the Dropdown would not work e.g.), but the interactivity of the `plotly` plots will still be available, since the HTML export retains the JavaScript functionality.
1. Use Quarto to generate a more polished report. Export your report as a PDF and HTML document.
   Use [this documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/tools/jupyter-lab.html) as a starting point.
1. Reflect on the entire analysis: What were the key findings? What surprised you? What would you investigate next?
:::
